title: Amoxicillin-treated green-synthesized iron oxide nanoparticles from  Artemisia absinthium  L.: UV-vis behaviour over 26 weeks, antioxidant activity and preliminary MCF-7 cytotoxicity
content: Green synthesis of iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs) with prolonged dispersion stability remains a challenge for biomedical applications. Here, IONPs were synthesized using Libyan wormwood (Artemisia absinthium L.) leaf extract and combined with amoxicillin at pH 8 to obtain IONPs–Amoxi. Notably, the unbound drug fraction was not quantified, and the corresponding supernatants were not retained. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) revealed an average core diameter of 39.5 ± 24 nm, while dynamic light scattering (DLS) indicated a hydrodynamic diameter of 47 ± 3.5 nm. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) showed spectral features consistent with interactions between amoxicillin functional groups and the nanoparticle surface. The zeta potential was −83.97 mV. During 26 weeks of storage under ambient conditions, no visible precipitation was observed, although UV-vis absorption intensity decreased over time, indicating a degree of optical aging. In preliminary antioxidant testing, IONPs–Amoxi exhibited concentration-dependent DPPH radical-scavenging activity, reaching 92.6% inhibition at 500 µg mL−1, compared with 99.3% for ascorbic acid. In an MTT assay against MCF-7 breast cancer cells, the formulation produced 88.28% cytotoxicity at 25 µg mL−1, with a reported IC50 of approximately 3.66 µg mL−1. These findings suggest the feasibility of plant-mediated IONP fabrication and indicate promising preliminary antioxidant and in vitro cytotoxic profiles. Further studies involving matched nanoparticle controls, quantitative drug-association analysis, release kinetics, comprehensive storage characterization, and mechanistic assays are required to fully clarify the contributions of the formulation components.
